title: Sectionwise presheaf model for localization of a ring object
statement:
Let $C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], with presheaf values in a universe containing its objects and arrows. Give abelian sheaves the sheafified tensor product [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Let $R$ be a commutative ring object [sk-def-sfb-ring-object] and $t$ a global section of $R$, with restriction $t_U\in R(U)$ on each object $U$.

Define a presheaf of commutative rings $P$ by $P(U)=R(U)[1/t_U]$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Explicitly its elements are fractions $r/t_U^n$, for $r\in R(U)$ and $n\geq0$, with relation
$$r/t_U^n=r'/t_U^m\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\exists k\geq0:\ t_U^k(t_U^m r-t_U^n r')=0.$$
Addition and multiplication are $(r/t_U^n)+(r'/t_U^m)=(t_U^m r+t_U^n r')/t_U^{n+m}$ and $(r/t_U^n)(r'/t_U^m)=rr'/t_U^{n+m}$; restriction sends $r/t_U^n$ to $(r|_V)/t_V^n$ along $V\to U$.

The ring sheafification $aP$ [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], viewed as a commutative ring object with the sheafified tensor product, has a canonical ring map $\eta:R\to aP$, $r\mapsto r/1$. The section $\eta(t)$ is invertible. For every commutative ring object $D$ and ring map $f:R\to D$ such that $f(t)$ is invertible, there is a unique ring map $\widetilde f:aP\to D$ with $\widetilde f\eta=f$.

Consequently, if $j:R\to L$ is any ring map with this same universal property and with $j(t)$ invertible, there is a unique ring-object isomorphism $\gamma:aP\xrightarrow{\sim}L$ satisfying $\gamma\eta=j$. No nonzero-divisor assumption on $t$ and no enough-points assumption on $C$ is required.

source.place: Tag 0EMC, lemma-simple-invert, applied to the subpresheaf of powers of a global section; ring-object formulation via the sheafified tensor product.

proof.text: Use the section-ring reconstruction in [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] for each commutative ring object in the statement: the section product is $r s=\mu(r\otimes s)$ and the section unit is $\eta(1)$. Its size hypotheses hold because the coefficient universe contains the site data. Its monoidal-local-equivalence hypothesis follows from [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]: $a(q\otimes_p H)\cong a(q)\otimes a(H)$, so a map inverted by $a$ remains inverted after tensoring. An internal ring morphism is a sectionwise ring map by evaluating its multiplication and unit equations on $r\otimes s$ and $1$. Conversely, [det-def-sfb-ring-object-sheaf] gives the internal structure on every sheaf of rings and sends sheaf ring maps to internal ring morphisms. These operations recover the starting internal structure: its multiplication is the unique extension of the displayed sectionwise bilinear map through $a(R\otimes_pR)$, and its unit is the unique extension of $n\mapsto n\cdot1$ through $a(\underline{\mathbf Z})$, by [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Thus all subsequent sectionwise ring constructions and factorizations give exactly the ring-object constructions and factorizations asserted here.

source.place: Unique extension of the sectionwise multiplication and unit; section-ring reconstruction and its morphism equations.

proof.text: For each $U$ form the actual ring $R(U)[1/t_U]$ of [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Its fraction relation and addition and multiplication are exactly the formulas in the statement, with $0=0/1$ and $1=1/1$. For $v:V\to U$ write $\rho_v:R(U)\to R(V)$ for restriction. The map $\rho_v$ followed by $R(V)\to R(V)[1/t_V]$ sends $t_U$ to the invertible image of $t_V$, since $\rho_v(t_U)=t_V$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-away-universal-property] to obtain a ring map $P(v)$, whose fraction formula is $P(v)(r/t_U^n)=\rho_v(r)/t_V^n$. The identity restriction and $P(\mathrm{id})$ agree on every $r/1$; for composable $v,w$, $P(w)P(v)$ and $P(vw)$ agree on every $r/1$ by the presheaf law for $R$. The uniqueness clause of the same node proves both presheaf laws. Also $i_U:r\mapsto r/1$ commutes with restrictions, so these maps give a presheaf ring morphism $i:R\to P$.

source.place: Tag 00CO, definition-localization and its preceding fraction construction; Tag 00CP, proposition-universal-property-localization. Applied objectwise as in sites-modules.tex, Tag 0EMC.

proof.text: Let $\sigma:P\to aP$ be ring sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] and put $\eta=\sigma i$. This is a ring sheaf morphism because $R$ is already a sheaf. Apply [det-def-sfb-ring-object-sheaf] to equip the ring sheaf $aP$ with the commutative ring-object structure for the sheafified tensor product; by step 1 the map $\eta$ is an internal ring morphism from the original $R$. The sections $u_U=1/t_U\in P(U)$ commute with every restriction. In $P(U)$ one has $(t_U/1)u_U=u_U(t_U/1)=1$, by [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Applying $\sigma_U$ gives a compatible global inverse for $\eta(t)$ in $aP$.

source.place: Tag 0EMC, lemma-simple-invert (proof omitted); explicit argument for powers of a global section.

proof.text:
Let $f:R\to D$ be a ring-object morphism with $f(t)$ invertible. By step 1 it is a morphism of reconstructed ring sheaves, and its sectionwise maps are $f_U:R(U)\to D(U)$. A global inverse for $f(t)$ restricts to an inverse for $f_U(t_U)$ on every $U$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-away-universal-property] to obtain the unique ring homomorphism
$$g_U:P(U)\longrightarrow D(U),\qquad g_U(r/t_U^n)=f_U(r)f_U(t_U)^{-n}.$$
For $v:V\to U$, the two ring maps $D(v)g_U$ and $g_VP(v)$ from $P(U)$ to $D(V)$ agree on $r/1$: both values are $f_V(\rho_v(r))$ by naturality of $f$. The uniqueness clause of the same node makes these maps equal. Hence $(g_U)$ is a presheaf ring morphism $g:P\to D$ with $gi=f$.

source.place: Tag 0EMC, lemma-simple-invert (proof omitted); explicit argument for powers of a global section.

proof.text: The sheafification universal property [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], in commutative rings, extends $g$ uniquely to a ring sheaf morphism $\widetilde f:aP\to D$ with $\widetilde f\sigma=g$. Consequently $\widetilde f\eta=\widetilde f\sigma i=gi=f$. By [det-def-sfb-ring-object-sheaf] this is a ring-object morphism. If $h:aP\to D$ is any other ring-object morphism with $h\eta=f$, step 1 makes it a ring sheaf morphism; each $(h\sigma)_U:P(U)\to D(U)$ agrees with $f_U$ on $r/1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-away-universal-property] it equals $g_U$, so $h\sigma=g$. Uniqueness in sheafification then gives $h=\widetilde f$. This proves exactly the asserted ring-object universal property.

source.place: Tag 0EMC, lemma-simple-invert (proof omitted); explicit argument for powers of a global section.

proof.text: Apply step 5 with $D=L$ and $f=j$ to obtain $\gamma:aP\to L$ satisfying $\gamma\eta=j$. The assumed universal property of $j$ applied to $\eta:R\to aP$ gives $\delta:L\to aP$ with $\delta j=\eta$. Then $(\delta\gamma)\eta=\eta$, so uniqueness in step 5 gives $\delta\gamma=\mathrm{id}_{aP}$. Likewise $(\gamma\delta)j=j$, so uniqueness for $j$ gives $\gamma\delta=\mathrm{id}_L$. Thus $\gamma$ is an isomorphism, and step 5 also proves its asserted uniqueness. The argument used inversion only in the target of a ring map; it never cancelled a power of $t$ in $R$ and never used stalks or points of $C$.

The delivery has no new nodes. The statement is the base text verbatim plus two added definition citations, and stmt_deps matches. Source checked: Stacks sites-modules.tex 0EMC (lemma-simple-invert, proof 'Omitted'). Taking S = powers of t, 'local sections become invertible' is equivalent to a global inverse of f(t), so the item is that lemma restated for ring objects; tags 00CO and 00CP confirmed in tags/tags. Steps: (1) The section-ring reconstruction comes from the statement of def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence. Its 'monoidal local equivalences' hypothesis follows from the strong monoidality in sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor. Uniqueness of extension in det-def-sfb-ring-object-sheaf, through a(R⊗pR) and a(Z), recovers the original mu and eta. (2) Restrictions of P and both presheaf laws follow from the localization-away universal-property leaf; its uniqueness is checked on r/1. (3) sigma(1/t) inverts eta(t). I read aP as sheafification in commutative rings (allowed by def-weil-pbc-sheafification, and step 5 says so). (4) Naturality of the g_U is proved by uniqueness, not assumed. (5) Existence and uniqueness through sheafification are proved in the same morphism category. (6) Uniqueness of universal objects, genuinely elementary. Small cases: t=1; t=0 or nilpotent (Z/4, t=2) give the zero sheaf; the empty site works. Duplicate search over the side-live DAG: def-weil-pbc-ringed-section-localization and its citers are module-sheafification and derived-category statements, not this ring universal property, so same_as [] is right. The declared tool uses (det-def-sfb-ring-object-sheaf, the internal-abelian reconstruction) are accepted. No SGA citation. No cycle. proof_deps equals the union of uses.
